paragraphs: Rabbi Yose HaKohen: Avot 2:8; Mishnah, Eduyot 8:2. He was pious, as we say in Shabbat, chapter 1: Rabbi Yose HaKohen was pious. But our text there, 19a, beginning, has: ‘They said of Rabbi Yose HaKohen, and some say of Rabbi Yose HaChasid.’ Thus according to this reading, Rabbi Yose HaKohen appears not to be Rabbi Yose HaChasid. His handwriting was never found in a gentile’s possession; likewise in the Tosefta, chapter 14. He was Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai’s student. In Avot de-Rabbi Natan, chapter 14, Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai called Rabbi Yose HaKohen ‘the pious one of the generation.’ In Avot, chapter 2: Rabbi Yose HaKohen was pious. This is against Dorot Olam’s view that he was Rabbi Yose HaGelili; see his entry. Shalshelet HaKabbalah 27a writes that some say he was Yosef ben Guryon, Nakdimon’s brother. Chagigah, chapter 2, 14b: Rabbi Yehoshua—in the Jerusalem Talmud, Rabbi Shimon ben Netanel—and Rabbi Yose HaKohen were walking on the road. They said: ‘Let us too expound the Account of the Chariot.’ Rabbi Yehoshua began, and so forth; see his entry. Rabbi Yose HaKohen told Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai. Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai said: ‘Happy are you,’ and so forth; ‘you and I too, in my dream, were reclining on Mount Sinai. A heavenly voice came upon us, saying: Come up here! Great halls are prepared for you and great couches spread for you. You, your students, and your students’ students are destined for the third company sitting before the Divine Presence.’ Taavah LaEinayim there writes that Rabbi Yose HaKohen was Rabbi Yehoshua’s colleague. He is mentioned in the Mishnah only in Eduyot, chapter 8, where he testified with Zekharyah ben HaKatzav, his colleague. At the end of Moed Katan, 23a, his wife died. In Semachot, chapter 4, it was on the eve of Passover, and they made him impure against his will. He told her sister at the cemetery: ‘Go and care for your sister’s children.’ He married her immediately that day, but did not have intercourse with her for thirty days. In the Jerusalem Talmud this incident concerns Rabbi Tarfon; see his entry. Zevachim 100a: ‘An incident concerning Yosef HaKohen, whose wife died,’ and so forth. Avodah Zarah 13a, Eruvin 47b, beginning, and Jerusalem Talmud, Berakhot, chapter 3, mishnah 1: Rabbi Yose said, ‘An incident concerning Yosef HaKohen, who became impure and went after Rabbi to Sidon.’ This requires examination, for he preceded him by much. It appears they are one. Semachot, chapter 4: Yose HaBavli became impure and went outside the Land to learn with Rabbi Yose at Sidon. Rosh Hashanah 17b: Belurit the convert asked Rabban Gamliel; Rabbi Yose HaKohen attended to her and answered, and so forth, until Rabbi Akiva came and taught, and so forth. For his burial, see Rabbi Elazar ben Arakh.
